output.summary: The evidence leans hawkish for the 2026-12-09 decision. Although the Committee held at 3-3/4 to 4 percent in October, the two dissents were hawkish ("preferred to raise"), the September minutes note "most participants" expected "another increase ... would likely be appropriate by year end," and the SEP median (4.1) implies roughly one more quarter-point hike ("implied_change_bp: 22.5"). The statement upgraded growth to "a strong pace," inflation "remains elevated" (gap ~1.0pp), the Chair said "inflation is too high," and base-rate history after a hike shows a 0.653 hike probability and zero cut probability. The main offset is the softened, data-dependent guidance ("The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance"), which is why the net tilt is only modestly hawkish rather than strongly so.

output.summary: The balance of evidence leans hawkish for the December 9, 2026 decision. After a September hike to 3-3/4 to 4 percent, the Committee held in October on a 10-2 vote, with both dissenters (Cook and Hammack) preferring to raise further. Inflation is still described as elevated, the gap_pp measure is 1.008, inflation risks are seen as skewed to the upside, the Chairman says growth has strengthened, the SEP path implies 22.5bp of further change, the September minutes say most participants expected another increase by year-end, and conditional base rates after a hike put 0.653 probability on another hike. Counterweighing this, the Committee actually paused in October and moved to more patient, data-dependent language ('accumulation of more information'). Net: a modest hawkish tilt of +5bp. Note: there are no policy-related speeches in the period, so that channel is absent from the evidence.
